decision: Admit the bounded pre-registered same-backend experiment; this is not bitwise HF/vLLM or resume-trajectory equivalence.
rationale: Independent small FP32 dense-mask forward/gradient tests, 42 dynamic-shape cases and SP4 tests pass; real training and cache accounting use the same visibility rule.
Short and typical nonbinding windows have exactly the custom-Full CE. Their gradient relative L2 differences (0.0067755 and 0.0034254) are below native-repeat differences (0.0087280 and 0.0086431).

Custom Full versus native SDPA has CE differences 0.000005722 and 0.000346452; global gradient cosines 0.9997863 and 0.9998678. All 683 trainable parameters have finite gradients. These differences exceed same-implementation repeat noise and are not called bitwise equality.

All three trained groups share custom FlexAttention, full-parameter native CE, FP32 masters and BF16 computation; all quality comparisons share the native vLLM Triton backend and output-only penalty 1.02.

Across short/typical/long inference traces, window top-1 agreement is 99.02%-99.76%, with no disagreement at the original margin>0.5 criterion. All 28 HF reference caches are unchanged and physical storage/page bounds pass.

Raw fixed BF16 logit tolerances failed for native Full controls too and remain false in original reports. Penalized distributions and centered errors supplement, rather than replace, those raw reports.

Typical R128/R256 maximum KL 0.0169012 and TV 0.0910509 also occur in matched custom Full before the output window binds. Long R256 KL 0.0018453/TV 0.0270171 exceed matched native Full TV 0.0179105; this excess is explicitly retained. No assertion is made that every R-SWA error lies within its matched Full envelope.

Saved model, Adam, scheduler and all-rank RNG restoration are exact. Continued training is numerically non-bitwise; same-implementation native repeat trajectories also failed the strict initial trajectory tolerance. Original failures and measured noise controls are retained.
Pipeline operation passed on two Dev meetings, but the three-update engineering checkpoint fails functional quality. It is never used as a formal initialization or selected checkpoint.
limitations: Engineering inference coverage is three training meetings and finite traces, not a proof of exact equality on every future meeting.
KL/TV use saved logit positions; top-1 and high-margin checks cover the full saved trajectories.
Quality and speed gains remain unmeasured by the formal experiment; every failure remains in its scores.
Cold-cache timing API and forced-history instrumentation passed a 300-token check; the complete fixed-trajectory performance matrix remains pending.
